content:
IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE, PATIALA HOUSE COURTS, NEW DELHI
SUIT NO. 104 OF 2026

STATEMENT OF WITNESS: RAJESH SHARMA, S/O LATE SH. M.L. SHARMA, AGED 48 YEARS

1. I am the Senior Director of Operations at Nexus Infotech Private Limited.
2. On 14th August 2026, the Defendant Bharat Cloud Solutions LLP suffered an unannounced server outage lasting 18 hours.
3. The financial loss incurred by the Plaintiff due to SLA failure is ₹ 1,25,00,000 (Rupees One Crore Twenty Five Lakhs).
4. A legal notice dated 22nd August 2026 was served under Section 73 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
5. All server downtime timestamp logs have been stored on optical media and authenticated under Section 63 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

DEPONENT: Rajesh Sharma
VERIFICATION: Verified at New Delhi on this 24th day of October 2026 that the contents of paragraphs 1 to 5 are true and correct.

title: Cloud_Services_Agreement_Nexus_Bharat.txt
content:
ENTERPRISE CLOUD SERVICES AND DATA HOSTING AGREEMENT
BETWEEN:
Nexus Infotech Private Limited, having registered office at Connaught Place, New Delhi (Plaintiff / Service Recipient)
AND
Bharat Cloud Solutions LLP, having registered office at Cyber City, Gurugram (Defendant / Service Provider)

CLAUSE 1: DEFINITIONS & SCOPE OF SERVICES
1.1 The Service Provider agrees to provide high-availability distributed server infrastructure with guaranteed 99.98% uptime.
1.2 Any downtime exceeding 15 consecutive minutes shall be categorized as a Severity 1 Critical Outage.

CLAUSE 8: LIMITATION OF LIABILITY & INDEMNIFICATION
8.1 The total aggregate liability of the Service Provider for any breach of this Agreement shall be capped at the total fees paid in the immediately preceding one (1) month.
8.2 The Service Recipient agrees to unconditionally indemnify and hold harmless the Service Provider against any third-party claims, uncapped consequential damages, and data loss incidents.

CLAUSE 14: DISPUTE RESOLUTION & ARBITRATION
14.1 Any dispute arising out of or in connection with this agreement shall be referred to arbitration.
14.2 The Service Provider shall have the unilateral right and sole discretion to appoint the Sole Arbitrator.
14.3 The seat of arbitration shall be New Delhi, and the proceedings shall be governed by the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

CLAUSE 19: GOVERNING LAW AND EVIDENCE
19.1 This agreement is governed by the laws of India.
19.2 All system logs and server timestamps shall be authenticated in compliance with Section 63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

title: Anticipatory_Bail_Petition_Vikramaditya.txt
content:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT BOMBAY
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION NO. 1984 OF 2026

IN THE MATTER OF:
Mr. Vikramaditya Singhania
Residing at Altamount Road, Mumbai
...APPLICANT

VERSUS

State of Maharashtra & Anr.
...RESPONDENT

APPLICATION UNDER SECTION 482 OF THE BHARATIYA NAGARIK SURAKSHA SANHITA, 2023 (ERSTWHILE SECTION 438 OF THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE, 1973).

1. That the Applicant has genuine apprehension of arrest in C.R. No. 142/2026 registered at Cyber Crime Police Station under Section 318 and Section 316 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
2. That the dispute arises out of contractual disagreements regarding cryptocurrency escrow reconciliation.
3. That the Applicant relies upon 'Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI' (2022) 10 SCC 51 and 'Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar' (2014) 8 SCC 273.
4. That the applicant has submitted a Certificate under Section 63 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 verifying all digital wallet transactions.
